one_line: A cooperative bomb-defusal game where the human sees visual facts and the agent operates through deliberately limited WebMCP tools.
what_it_does: Presents a timed bomb with visual modules to the human while an agent reads rules/progress and performs narrowly scoped actions, requiring communication between both sides.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP is the core mechanic: the typed interface intentionally withholds visual facts while exposing reliable actions, creating a capability split that ordinary UI driving would undermine or make unreliable.
leverage_evidence: Description specifies seven tools, two read tools and five scoped actions.
get_bomb_status explicitly refuses to return wire colours and keypad symbols.
Human and agent watch calls/results live and neither can complete the intended tool-only run alone.
execution_rationale: The frame sheet shows a coherent timed game workspace and configured bomb/session UI, but no readable completed defusal or explicit tool trace is visible.
execution_evidence: Frame sheet visibly shows BLINDSPOT workspace, 5:00 timer, controls, and side status panel.
Packet reports a live demo and public repository.
No final success state or transcript is supplied.
impact_rationale: The game offers a clear, memorable learning experience about least-privilege agent interfaces and human-agent collaboration, though its audience is primarily experimental/game-oriented.
impact_evidence: Pitch defines a complete cooperative five-minute game loop.
About text frames the game as a playable demonstration of tool-contract design.
Visible product framing supports a deliberate cooperative experience.
creativity_rationale: Turning information withholding and interface-contract design into the central puzzle mechanic is unusually original and pursued coherently through the bomb-defusal format.
creativity_evidence: The human/agent capability split is the premise, not a presentation layer.
The game deliberately asks what a good tool contract should withhold.
Visual bomb interaction and typed agent actions are combined into one dependency loop.
usability_note: Clear role split and timer are legible, but the agent-only protocol and communication burden may be demanding for first-time users.
red_flags: No submitted video despite frame sheets; frame evidence lacks a completed result.
standouts: WebMCP least privilege is made playable and necessary.
advance_reason: Distinctive, high-leverage WebMCP concept with a coherent demonstrated game surface.

leverage_rationale: Structured configuration and shared observation state make the workflow more reliable than UI driving, but a general agent could reproduce much of the planning and navigation with friction.

execution_evidence: Frame sheet shows the six-step workflow and rendered sky-map UI.

No clearly readable final star list or comparison result is visible.
impact_rationale: It addresses a concrete beginner stargazing friction: deciding what, when, and where to observe, then capturing the experience. The educational and family use case is credible.
impact_evidence: About text identifies location/time/visibility planning barriers.
Workflow produces a printable guide and supports recording actual observations.

creativity_rationale: The agent-plans/human-observes/record-and-compare loop is a fresh synthesis for astronomy education, though the underlying guide category is familiar.

red_flags: No explicit tool invocation is readable in the frame evidence.
standouts: Strong bridge from digital planning to real-world observation.
advance_reason: Credible educational workflow with meaningful shared state and clear audience value.

one_line: An agent-assisted reader that keeps immutable source text separate from human marks and attributed, removable agent marginalia.
what_it_does: Adapts reading density to what the user knows, adds glosses/connections/citations in a separate margin layer, and lets the reader confirm proposed knowledge and remove agent artifacts.
leverage_rationale: The agent operates inside a shared, persistent reading state while preserving source integrity and attribution; this is substantially more precise than a chat sidebar or generic UI driving.
leverage_evidence: About text describes separate source, user, and agent layers.
Agent records proposed knowledge that the human confirms with a tap.
Tools reshape the same document around section-level knowledge state.
execution_rationale: The concept is detailed and intentional, but there are no frame sheets and the packet provides no directly checkable runtime evidence, capping execution confidence.
execution_evidence: Detailed description specifies reader, knowledge confirmation, folding, expansion, and artifact removal.
Packet reports a live demo but no video and no submitted frame sheets.
Devpost screenshot is packaging evidence only and cannot prove operation.
impact_rationale: Readers, researchers, and learners have a credible need for context-aware annotation and knowledge scaffolding without contaminating source text.
impact_evidence: Description identifies the limitation of generic chat beside documents.

creativity_rationale: The epistemological margin and three-layer reading model are memorable, with a strong interaction concept for human-agent collaboration in documents.
creativity_evidence: Agent artifacts live in a reversible margin rather than rewriting the source.

usability_note: Layer toggles and confirmation affordances suggest good control, but adaptive density could be cognitively complex.
red_flags: No frame sheets or video; execution claims are not visually verifiable.
About text explicitly references prior projects, indicating pre-existing conceptual lineage.
standouts: Source/user/agent separation is a principled and memorable interaction model.
advance_reason: Exceptional concept and credible impact, despite thin execution evidence.

one_line: A browser-based MuJoCo reinforcement-learning lab where an agent and human jointly configure, train, inspect, and deploy a MicroDuck policy.

leverage_rationale: RL diagnosis benefits from structured access to metrics, reward decomposition, curriculum and config state while the human judges behavior visually; 53 tools make repeatable shared experimentation practical.

standouts: Strong treatment of revision integrity, approval, idempotency, and partial failure.
